settings.general.title: Preferences
settings.general.subtitle: Language and theme.
settings.language.label: Language
settings.language.hint: Changes apply immediately; open windows, tooltips and menus update together.
settings.language.detail:
Only the interface is translated. Data folder names, logs, JSON fields and internal ids stay unchanged so existing data keeps working.
Switching languages does not restart the app and does not change work profiles, startup plans, icon layouts or the recycle bin.
settings.appearance.resetHint: Preferences reset. Language and theme were applied immediately.
settings.theme.label: Theme
settings.theme.hint: Light / Dark / Follow Windows; changes apply immediately.
settings.theme.detail:
Only interface colors and the window title bar change. Icon layouts, profiles and other data are not modified.
Changes apply immediately to open windows, tooltips and dialogs.
Follow Windows uses the Windows app theme.
settings.priority.startupFirst: Restore the Startup & Restore work profile first
settings.priority.applicationsFirst: Start the Startup Apps plan first
settings.tip.resetDragSpeed.name: Reset speed
settings.tip.resetDragSpeed.title: Reset speed
settings.tip.resetDragSpeed.description: Restore the drag auto-scroll speed to the default 1.0×.
settings.resetSection.label: Reset this section
settings.resetSection.title: Reset this section
settings.resetSection.short: Only this section returns to defaults; other sections are unaffected.
settings.resetSection.detail: Only this section is reset; saved work profiles, startup plans and icon layouts are not deleted.
settings.resetSection.noneShort: This section has no settings yet; new settings will appear here.
settings.resetSection.noneDetail: This section has no resettable settings yet.
settings.resetSection.confirmMessageForm: Reset the settings in "{0}" to defaults? Other sections are unaffected.
settings.resetAll.label: Reset all settings
settings.resetAll.confirmBody:
Reset every setting to defaults?
This resets all options in General, Startup & Restore, Icon Layouts, Startup Apps, Shortcuts and Preferences (drag speed, start with Windows, startup priority, per-section switches and waits, custom shortcuts, language, theme and so on).
Not deleted: saved work profiles, startup plans, icon layouts or recycle bin contents.
This cannot be undone.
settings.resetAll.done: All settings were reset to defaults; profiles and icon layouts were untouched.
settings.shortcuts.copyProfile.title: Copy the current profile or icon layout
settings.shortcuts.copyProfile.descripti: Copy the current selection to the clipboard: in Startup & Restore it copies the work profile, in Startup Apps it copies the startup plan (including its items), and in Icon Layouts it copies the current layout (including icon positions and the desktop preview). Press Ctrl+V for an independent copy. Inside a text box these keys still perform normal copy and paste.
settings.shortcuts.pasteProfile.title: Paste a profile or layout copy
settings.shortcuts.pasteProfile.descript: Paste a copied profile or layout as a new copy (duplicate names get a numeric suffix) and undo it with Ctrl+Z. Work profiles, startup plans and icon layouts stay in their own workspaces and never cross over.
settings.shortcuts.undo.title: Undo
settings.shortcuts.undo.description: Undo the most recent change (all four workspaces share one undo history): sorting, checking, adding, deleting, renaming or appending time in Startup & Restore; adding, removing, sorting, enabling, renaming or deleting plans in Startup Apps; restoring or permanently deleting recycle bin items; saving or restoring icon layouts.
settings.shortcuts.redo.title: Redo
settings.shortcuts.shiftDrag.title: Drag to reorder directly
settings.shortcuts.shiftDrag.description:
Hold the configured drag prefix and drag a list item or plan card directly to reorder or move it without using the ≡ handle on the right. The ≡ handle always drags with the left button.
Applies to: Startup & Restore / Startup Apps / Icon Layouts. The icon layout editor is not a list drag and is not affected.
settings.shortcuts.confirmEnter.title: Confirm (same as Yes)
settings.shortcuts.confirmEnter.descript: Pressing Enter in any confirmation dialog is the same as clicking Yes. Esc or the close button still means No. On the restore card, Enter is the same as Immediate Restore during the countdown, or Continue Restore in the CPU/memory load prompt.
settings.shortcuts.closeEsc.title: Close the dialog (same as No)
settings.shortcuts.closeEsc.description: Pressing Esc or clicking the close button in any confirmation dialog means No and never confirms by accident. On the restore card, Esc is the same as Cancel Restore.
settings.shortcuts.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
settings.shortcuts.subtitle: These shortcuts work throughout the app. Double-click a keycap or click the pencil to edit, right-click a keycap to copy its keys, plus to add, and the trash to delete. Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V stay normal copy and paste inside text boxes.
settings.shortcuts.short: These shortcuts work throughout the app and can be edited, deleted or added; double-click a keycap to edit.
settings.shortcuts.countFormat: {0} commands, {1} shortcuts; all work throughout the app.
settings.shortcuts.emptyHint: Click it or the plus to add
settings.shortcuts.pressHint: Press a key combination to change
settings.shortcuts.capAccessibleFormat: Shortcut {0}; double-click to edit this shortcut.
settings.shortcuts.deleted: That one shortcut was deleted; other bindings were kept.
settings.shortcuts.restored: This command is back to its default shortcut.

settings.shortcuts.pager.previous.title: Previous page

settings.shortcuts.pager.rows.descriptio: Choose 5, 10, 25 or 50 rows. The default is 10; your choice is remembered.
settings.shortcuts.search.title: Search shortcuts
settings.shortcuts.search.description: Search by command name, key binding or summary. Separate multiple words with spaces; all must match.
settings.shortcuts.edit.tipDescription: Open the recording dialog, press the new combination and save.
settings.shortcuts.delete.tipDescription: Delete only this binding; other bindings and the defaults stay unchanged.
settings.shortcuts.add.tipTitle: Add a shortcut to this command
settings.shortcuts.add.tipDescription: Open the recording dialog and save a combination; a command can have several shortcuts.
settings.shortcuts.restore.tipTitle: Restore this command to its default
settings.shortcuts.restore.tipDescriptio: Only this command goes back to its default shortcut; other commands stay unchanged.
settings.shortcuts.dialog.editBody: Set a shortcut for the following action:
settings.shortcuts.dialog.addBody: Add a shortcut for the following action:
settings.shortcuts.resetAll.label: Reset all shortcuts
settings.shortcuts.resetAll.short: Restore all shortcuts and the drag gesture to their defaults; other settings stay unchanged.
settings.shortcuts.resetAll.detail: Only bindings on the shortcuts page are reset (including the drag prefix and mouse button). Work profiles, startup plans, icon layouts and all other settings are kept.
settings.shortcuts.resetAll.confirmMessa: Restore all shortcuts and the drag gesture to their defaults? Other settings will not be affected.
settings.shortcuts.resetAll.done: All shortcuts are back to their defaults.
settings.shortcuts.error.onlyModifier: Modifier keys alone are not a shortcut; press a main key too.
settings.shortcuts.error.reservedFormat: {0} is reserved for confirm, cancel or keyboard focus.
settings.shortcuts.error.unknownCommand: This command could not be found. Reopen the settings page.
settings.shortcuts.error.duplicateFormat: {0} is already a shortcut of "{1}". Choose another combination.
settings.shortcuts.error.conflictFormat: {0} is already used by "{1}". Choose another combination.

settings.shortcuts.drag.saved: Drag settings saved and active immediately.
settings.shortcuts.drag.restored: Drag restored to Shift + left button.
settings.shortcuts.drag.error.noPrefix: Hold a key combination first (Ctrl / Alt / Shift or a letter key).

settings.shortcuts.drag.capAccessibleFor: Drag {0}; double-click to edit the drag settings.
settings.shortcuts.drag.edit.tipTitle: Edit the drag prefix and mouse button
settings.shortcuts.drag.edit.tipDescript: Press a key combination, then click Left drag or Right drag; if you do not click a mouse button, the current one is kept. The ≡ handle always drags with the left button.
settings.shortcuts.drag.restore.tipDescr: Only the drag prefix and mouse button are reset; keyboard shortcuts are untouched.
settings.about.title: About
settings.about.description: Version, project home and update checks.
settings.about.tagline: Saves and restores startup items, desktop icon layouts and startup apps.
settings.about.author: Author
settings.about.notConfiguredHint: Configure the GitHub repository and author email to enable update checks and contact links.
settings.about.footerHint: Configure the project home and author email to show the project and email links here.
settings.about.suppressed: Update checks are disabled in test mode.
settings.about.updateHint: Checking for updates only opens the download page; nothing is downloaded or installed automatically.
settings.about.updateDialogMessageFormat: Current version {0}, latest version {1}. Open the download page?
settings.help.startupAutoRestore.title: Restore work profile after launch
settings.help.startupAutoRestore.short: Restore the last saved work profile when the app opens.
settings.help.startupAutoRestore.detail:
Each time the app opens, it restores the apps, folders and web pages saved in the current profile, so you do not need to click Restore Now.
This is independent of General → Start with Windows: that setting only opens the app; this one performs the restore. With both on, Windows sign-in opens the app and restores once.
Reopening the app during the same Windows session does not restore again; only after a restart does it restore once.
settings.help.scanTerminals.title: Scan terminals and local URLs
settings.help.scanTerminals.short: Also record terminal windows and local URLs when saving (they cannot be restored).
settings.help.scanTerminals.detail:
When saving, record terminal windows (cmd, PowerShell, Windows Terminal, etc.) and local URLs (localhost, 127.0.0.1, file:, etc.) in addition to apps, folders and web pages.
Note: Startup & Restore cannot restore these (for example a dsh terminal or ComfyUI at 127.0.0.1:8188). When enabled, the save notice names the items that cannot be restored.
To keep them available after sign-in, add them to Startup Apps. Off by default.
settings.help.loadGate.title: Wait under high load
settings.help.loadGate.short: Wait when the PC is busy instead of forcing items to start.
settings.help.loadGate.detail:
Before starting each item, check CPU and memory. If either is above the limit below, wait until it drops, then continue. This avoids making startup slower.
CPU Limit and CPU Wait Limit live in General and are shared by every startup workspace. This switch enables them.
settings.help.startupInitialDelay.title: Wait before start (seconds)
settings.help.startupInitialDelay.short: Wait a few seconds before restoring to give the system time to settle.
settings.help.startupInitialDelay.detail:
When you click Restore Now or automatic restore runs, wait this many seconds before starting items. This gives a freshly started or signed-in system some breathing room.
Allowed range: 0–60 seconds. 0 starts immediately; maximum 60.
settings.help.startupItemDelay.title: Item interval (seconds)
settings.help.startupItemDelay.short: Pause this long between starting items.
settings.help.startupItemDelay.detail:
Restore starts items one by one. After each item, wait this long before starting the next.
Too small can overload CPU or memory; too large makes restore slow. 0 means no wait.
settings.help.startupWebDelay.title: Web page interval (seconds)
settings.help.startupWebDelay.short: How long to pause between opening web pages.
settings.help.startupWebDelay.detail:
During restore, browser pages open one by one. Wait this long between pages to avoid freezing the browser.
Default 0.5 seconds. 0 means no wait, but pages still open one at a time (closing the window is the only way to skip the rest of that window's pages).
settings.help.applicationsAutoRestore.sh: Restore the checked items in the current startup plan when the app opens.
settings.help.applicationsAutoRestore.de:
On the first launch after a restart, restore the checked items in the current startup plan. Reopening during the same session does not start them again; already running items are skipped.
Independent of Startup & Restore automatic restore. If both run, General → Startup priority decides the order.
settings.help.applicationsWaitForLoad.sh: Wait when the PC is busy while restoring a startup plan.
settings.help.applicationsWaitForLoad.de:
Before starting each startup item, check CPU. If it is above General → CPU Limit, wait until it drops.
The wait limit is General → CPU Wait Limit.
settings.help.applicationsInitialDelay.s: Wait a few seconds before restoring the startup plan.
settings.help.applicationsInitialDelay.d:
Automatic restore and manual Restore Now both wait this many seconds before starting items.
Allowed range: 0–60 seconds. 0 starts immediately; maximum 60.
settings.help.applicationsItemDelay.shor: Pause this long between startup items.
settings.help.applicationsItemDelay.deta:
Startup plan items start one by one. After each item, wait this long before the next.
0 means no wait.
settings.help.applicationsWebDelay.title: Web page interval (seconds)
settings.help.applicationsWebDelay.short: How long to pause between restoring web pages.
settings.help.applicationsWebDelay.detai:
Applies only to web page items. Wait this long after opening each page.
Ignored when the plan has no web pages. 0 means no wait, but pages still open one at a time.
settings.help.layoutAutoRestore.title: Restore icon layout after launch
settings.help.layoutAutoRestore.short: Restore the current display's icon layout when the app opens.
settings.help.layoutAutoRestore.detail:
Affects Icon Layouts only. When the app opens, restore the last selected layout for the current display combination.
Completely independent of the similarly named switches in Startup & Restore and Startup Apps. Off by default.
settings.help.layoutInitialDelay.title: Wait before start (seconds)
settings.help.layoutInitialDelay.short: Wait a few seconds before restoring the icon layout.
settings.help.layoutInitialDelay.detail:
Affects only Icon Layouts automatic restore. After the app opens or the display configuration changes, wait this many seconds before restoring icon positions.
Allowed range: 0–60 seconds. 0 starts immediately; default 5.
settings.help.startupNewName.title: New work profile name
settings.help.startupNewName.short: Used when creating a new profile in Startup & Restore.
settings.help.startupNewName.detail:
Used when you click Save current profile or right-click New blank profile. Duplicate names get a Windows-style “(2)” suffix.
Leave empty to use the default “Work Profile”. This only affects profiles created later; existing profiles keep their names.
settings.help.applicationsNewName.title: New startup plan name
settings.help.applicationsNewName.short: Used when creating a new startup plan.
settings.help.applicationsNewName.detail:
Used when you right-click New blank plan. Duplicate names get a Windows-style “(2)” suffix.
Leave empty to use the default “Startup Plan”. This only affects plans created later; existing plans keep their names.
settings.help.layoutNewName.title: New icon layout name
settings.help.layoutNewName.short: Used when saving a new icon layout.
settings.help.layoutNewName.detail:
Used when you click Save icon layout or right-click New layout. Duplicate names get a Windows-style “(2)” suffix.
Leave empty to use the default “Icon layout”. This only affects layouts created later; New folder still asks for its own name.
settings.help.generalScrollSpeed.title: Drag auto-scroll speed
settings.help.generalScrollSpeed.short: How fast lists auto-scroll while dragging; shared by all three workspaces.
settings.help.generalScrollSpeed.detail:
When you drag items in a list or move the pointer to the top or bottom edge, the list auto-scrolls at this speed.
This is global: Startup & Restore, Icon Layouts and Startup Apps share one value, so one change applies everywhere.
1.0× is the default; lower is steadier, higher is faster.
settings.help.autoStart.title: Start with Windows
settings.help.autoStart.short: Open this app after Windows sign-in, without restoring anything.
settings.help.autoStart.detail:
When enabled, Windows starts Workspace Restorer at sign-in. It only opens the app and does not restore any plan.
To restore a work profile as well, enable Restore work profile after launch in Startup & Restore.
The switches are independent: this one only opens the app; both together open and restore.
settings.help.startupPriority.title: Startup priority
settings.help.startupPriority.short: Which side runs first when both automatic restores are enabled.
settings.help.startupPriority.detail:
When Startup & Restore and Startup Apps both have automatic restore enabled, this decides the order.
It has no effect when only one side is enabled.
settings.help.resetAll.title: Reset all settings
settings.help.resetAll.short: Restore every section to defaults without touching saved content.
settings.help.resetAll.detail:
Restores all settings in General, Startup & Restore, Icon Layouts, Startup Apps and Preferences to their defaults.
The Shortcuts page only displays keys and has nothing to reset.
Saved work profiles, startup plans, icon layouts and the recycle bin are not deleted. A confirmation appears before anything changes.
settings.help.cpuLimit.title: CPU limit (%)
settings.help.cpuLimit.short: Pause restore when CPU is above this value before starting an item; shared by all startup workspaces.
settings.help.cpuLimit.detail:
Before starting each item, if CPU usage is above this percentage, pause and ask whether to continue.
Shared by Startup & Restore, Startup Apps and future startup features. Only effective when the matching Wait under high load switch is on.
settings.help.cpuWait.title: CPU wait limit (seconds)
settings.help.cpuWait.short: Maximum wait when CPU stays high; restore pauses automatically when reached.
settings.help.cpuWait.detail:
If CPU stays above the limit, wait at most this many seconds. If it is still high, pause restore instead of forcing it.
0 means no CPU wait. Shared by startup workspaces.
settings.help.memoryLimit.title: Memory limit (%)
settings.help.memoryLimit.short: Pause restore when memory is above this value before starting an item; shared by all startup workspaces.
settings.help.memoryLimit.detail:
Before starting each item, if memory usage is above this percentage, pause restore and show a prompt.
Shared by Startup & Restore, Startup Apps and future startup features. Only effective when the matching Wait under high load switch is on.
settings.help.memoryWait.title: Memory wait limit (seconds)
settings.help.memoryWait.short: Maximum wait when memory stays high; restore pauses automatically when reached.
settings.help.memoryWait.detail:
When memory is above the limit, wait for it to drop before continuing. If it stays high for this many seconds, pause restore to avoid making the PC sluggish.
0 means no wait and pause immediately. Shared by startup workspaces.
settings.tip.applicationsAutoRestore.des: Checked: on the first launch after a restart, restore the current startup plan once.
settings.tip.applicationsAutoRestore.sug: Reopening during the same session does not start items again; already running items are skipped. This is independent of Startup & Restore automatic restore.
settings.tip.applicationsWaitForLoad.des: Checked: wait when the PC is busy before starting startup plan items.
settings.tip.applicationsWaitForLoad.sug: CPU Limit and CPU Wait Limit come from General; this switch only enables them.
settings.tip.layoutAutoRestore.name: Restore icon layout after launch
settings.tip.layoutAutoRestore.title: Restore icon layout after launch
settings.tip.layoutAutoRestore.descripti: Affects Icon Layouts only; off by default and independent of the Startup & Restore / Startup Apps switches.
settings.tip.layoutAutoRestore.suggestio: When the app opens, restore the current display's icon layout; display changes use the same switch and pre-start wait.
settings.tip.layoutInitialDelay.name: Wait before start (seconds)
settings.tip.layoutInitialDelay.title: Wait before start (seconds)
settings.tip.layoutInitialDelay.suggesti: Affects only Icon Layouts automatic restore: after opening the app or a display change, wait this long before restoring icon positions.
settings.tip.cpuLimit.name: CPU limit (%)
settings.tip.cpuLimit.title: CPU limit (%)
settings.tip.cpuLimit.suggestion: Too low (for example 50) waits constantly; 100 means no limit. Only effective when Wait under high load is on.
settings.tip.cpuWait.name: CPU wait limit (seconds)
settings.tip.cpuWait.title: CPU wait limit (seconds)
settings.tip.cpuWait.description: Integer from 0 to 3600; 30–120 seconds is common.
settings.tip.cpuWait.suggestion: If CPU stays above the limit, wait at most this long, then pause restore instead of forcing it. 0 means no wait.
settings.tip.memoryLimit.name: Memory limit (%)
settings.tip.memoryLimit.title: Memory limit (%)
settings.tip.memoryLimit.suggestion: Before each item, if memory is above this percentage, pause restore and ask whether to continue. Only effective when the matching Wait under high load is on.
settings.tip.memoryWait.name: Memory wait limit (seconds)
settings.tip.memoryWait.title: Memory wait limit (seconds)
settings.tip.memoryWait.suggestion: When memory is above the limit, wait for it to drop; if it stays high, pause restore automatically. 0 means no wait and pause immediately.
settings.tip.startupInitialDelay.name: Wait before start (seconds)
settings.tip.startupInitialDelay.title: Wait before start (seconds)
settings.tip.startupInitialDelay.descrip: Integer from 0 to 60; 5–10 seconds is common.
settings.tip.startupInitialDelay.suggest: Both automatic restore and Restore Now wait first; about 5 seconds is steadier, 0 starts immediately.
settings.tip.startupItemDelay.name: Item interval (seconds)
settings.tip.startupItemDelay.title: Item interval (seconds)
settings.tip.startupItemDelay.descriptio: Integer from 0 to 600; 2–5 seconds is common.
settings.tip.startupItemDelay.suggestion: Use 3–5 seconds for many items or a slower PC; 0 starts items back to back.
settings.tip.startupWebDelay.name: Web page interval (seconds)
settings.tip.startupWebDelay.title: Web page interval (seconds)
settings.tip.startupWebDelay.suggestion: Use 1 second with many tabs to avoid freezing the browser; 0 still opens pages one at a time.
settings.tip.applicationsInitialDelay.de: Integer from 0 to 60; 5–10 seconds is common.
settings.tip.applicationsInitialDelay.su: Affects Startup Apps only; manual Restore Now also waits first, matching Startup & Restore; 0 starts immediately.
settings.tip.applicationsItemDelay.name: Item interval (seconds)
settings.tip.applicationsItemDelay.title: Item interval (seconds)
settings.tip.applicationsItemDelay.descr: Integer from 0 to 600; 2–5 seconds is common.
settings.tip.applicationsItemDelay.sugge: Pause after each item so everything does not launch at once and stall the PC.
settings.tip.applicationsWebDelay.name: Web page interval (seconds)
settings.tip.applicationsWebDelay.title: Web page interval (seconds)
settings.tip.applicationsWebDelay.sugges: Applies only to web pages; ignored when the plan has no web pages.
settings.tip.profileName.name: New work profile name
settings.tip.profileName.title: New work profile name
settings.tip.profileName.description: Used when creating a new work profile; empty means “Work Profile”.
settings.tip.profileName.suggestion: Only affects profiles created later; rename existing profiles by double-clicking the card title or using the context menu.
settings.tip.applicationsNewName.name: New startup plan name
settings.tip.applicationsNewName.title: New startup plan name
settings.tip.applicationsNewName.descrip: Used when creating a new startup plan; empty means “Startup Plan”.
settings.tip.applicationsNewName.suggest: Only affects plans created later; rename existing plans by double-clicking the card title or using the context menu.
settings.tip.layoutNewName.name: New icon layout name
settings.tip.layoutNewName.title: New icon layout name
settings.tip.layoutNewName.description: Used when saving a new icon layout; empty means “Icon layout”.
settings.tip.layoutNewName.suggestion: Only affects layouts created later; New folder still asks for its own name.
settings.tip.autoStart.name: Start with Windows
settings.tip.autoStart.title: Start with Windows
settings.tip.autoStart.description: Checked: open this app after Windows sign-in. Unchecked: do not start with Windows.
settings.tip.autoStart.suggestion: It only opens the app and restores nothing. To restore too, enable automatic restore in Startup & Restore.
settings.tip.startupAutoRestore.name: Restore work profile after launch
settings.tip.startupAutoRestore.title: Restore work profile after launch
settings.tip.startupAutoRestore.descript: Checked: restore the current profile once each time the app opens.
settings.tip.startupAutoRestore.suggesti: Reopening during the same session does not restore again; only after a restart does it restore once. It is independent of Start with Windows.
settings.tip.loadGate.name: Wait under high load
settings.tip.loadGate.title: Wait under high load
settings.tip.loadGate.description: Checked: wait when the PC is busy before starting items.
settings.tip.loadGate.suggestion: CPU Limit and CPU Wait Limit are only effective when this switch is on.
settings.tip.scanTerminals.name: Scan terminals and local URLs
settings.tip.scanTerminals.title: Scan terminals and local URLs
settings.tip.scanTerminals.description: Checked: also record terminal windows and local URLs when saving (they cannot be restored).
settings.tip.scanTerminals.suggestion: Off by default: Startup & Restore cannot restore these. To keep them after sign-in, add them to Startup Apps.
settings.tip.applicationsAutoStart.name: Start startup plan after launch
settings.tip.applicationsAutoStart.title: Start startup plan after launch
settings.tip.applicationsAutoStart.descr: Checked: start the current startup plan once each time the app opens.
settings.tip.applicationsAutoStart.sugge: Already running items are skipped; this is independent of Startup & Restore automatic restore.
settings.tip.dragScrollSpeedValue.descri: Click to type a multiplier directly (0.5–3, two decimal places).
settings.tip.dragScrollSpeedSlider.name: Drag auto-scroll speed
settings.tip.dragScrollSpeedSlider.title: Drag auto-scroll speed
settings.tip.dragScrollSpeedSlider.descr: Drag the slider to change the multiplier; the current value appears on the right. Click the value to type it directly (0.5–3, two decimal places).
settings.tip.dragScrollSpeedSlider.sugge: 1.0× is the default; lower is steadier, higher is faster. Click ↻ on the right to reset to 1.0×.
settings.tip.resetAll.name: Reset all settings
settings.tip.resetAll.title: Reset all settings
settings.tip.resetAll.description: Clicking asks for confirmation first; after confirming, all settings return to defaults without deleting saved profiles or icon layouts.
settings.tip.startupPriority.name: Startup priority
settings.tip.startupPriority.title: Startup priority
settings.tip.startupPriority.description: When both automatic restores are on, choose which runs first.
settings.tip.startupPriority.suggestion: It has no effect when only one side is enabled.
